title_options: JetBrains ACP Install Failed? Seven Checks Before Reinstalling
JetBrains ACP Install Failed: Find the Failing Layer Before You Reinstall
package_install_failed in JetBrains ACP: A Seven-Check Pre-Flight
presentation.title_rationale: The reader arrives holding one generic log token and a failed install, and the useful next move is an ordered check rather than a reinstall. The selected title frontloads the product and the reader's own words ('JetBrains ACP Install Failed?') and then promises one supported benefit: seven checks, which is exactly the numbered pre-flight the body delivers. At 62 characters it drops the method-and-year clutter of the previous 96-character headline ('What ... Log Line Actually Tells You (2026)'), which promised an interpretation of the log line before the article's actual deliverable. No figure, build number or success claim is in the title, so nothing in it outruns the evidence.
presentation.visual_purpose: The cover is a three-step conceptual map of the article's argument: the error token identifies a package (01), the failing layer lives in the registry/artifact contract (02), and the reader resolves it with an ordered pre-flight (03). It explains structure only; it carries no measured values, no counts and no vendor marks, and its footer labels it a conceptual checklist rather than measurement data. Evidence scope is the article body's own string anatomy, the registry FORMAT.md/README contract and the seven numbered checks, plus the published six-case loopback run for the claim that one token can hide five distinct defects.
